sourceText: Aster did not announce the night’s theme. She opened the LEGUIN-GETHEN sector and let the children discover for themselves which of the world’s rules concerned them directly. Marae lives in the body of a society without two permanent sexual roles. The memorial bore the name of Ursula K. Le Guin — The Left Hand of Darkness precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. Biology had to be treated as political infrastructure. A body capable of breathing another atmosphere, not aging, or sharing a mind with another species immediately produces new classes of obligation and new definitions of personhood. Orin perceived counterfactual costs as absences with weight. He did not confuse an unrealized branch with a victim, but he refused to let success rewrite rejected options as if they had been inevitable all along. 149 Rho was the first inhabitant to contradict them. Rho had neither access to their archives nor any interest in hyperdimensional pedagogy; there was a local problem, with deadlines, relatives, and consequences. For Rho, the speculative mechanism was not an ‘idea.’ It was the environment in which one had to decide what one was willing to risk losing. The problem closed quickly around them: Kesh searches for a simple social causality and finds that the same biology has produced different institutions in different regions. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Ge — Designed Genome: bodies and traits are designed; Mf — Multispecies Federation: different species share institutions. Course references included biotech SF; pluralist SF. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Tern broke the first consensus. ‘Sometimes the ethical question is whether we are entitled to know enough to optimize.’ Kesh answered without raising their voice: ‘If the element explains everything, we do not have an element. We have a word that has eaten the problem.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. 150 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS The White Hunger appeared in Aster as a loss of relief. She did not lack entertainment. She lacked the resistance of things to the model. When she could anticipate every reaction, the world became functionally an extension of her own mind, and the presence of the other thinned toward simulacrum. Marae remained in the local body when the others opened their protections. The gesture cost her: she felt cold, pressure, and physiological delay at exactly the scale the inhabitants felt them. “Otherwise we risk confusing the fact that we survive with the claim that the situation is bearable,” she said after catching her breath. The night did not end in victory. The Table separates the biological element from the history that turns it into society. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. While Kesh closed the record, Tern compared the sector’s noise with the anomaly detected in the Vinge zone. The pattern reappeared, but only in worlds where Aster’s control weakened. The correlation was unpleasant: either someone was calling him from outside, or his own need for an outside was learning to forge evidence. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the GENESIS operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — allows a system to create new agents, worlds, laws, or substrates — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, 151 and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. In the hall between sectors, Aster’s Hunger returned. None of the children tried to soothe it. They had begun to believe that some pains should not immediately be turned into demands upon the people nearby. 152 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
